winners.why_winner: All three candidates fail the realistic PF >= 1.3 floor (1.15 / 1.15 / 1.12). winners.why_winner: None of the three candidates clear the required bar of critic-realistic PF >= 1.3. Candidate 1 (vix_gated_keltner) lands at PF 1.25 with 12+ tunable knobs (high overfit) AND a critic-confirmed signal-count collapse (<10/yr across 20 ETFs → n>=100 takes 5+ years, violating Goal #1's need for trustworthy sample size on a 24-month horizon). Candidate 2 (breadth_thrust_rotation) lands at PF 1.25 / WR 46% — borderline-but-fails the PF floor, plus the critic flagged the 4w mean-reversion overlay (0.2 weight) as likely noise and the 0.5/0.3/0.2 composite weights as unjustified free parameters; cross-sectional momentum on sector SPDRs is also the most front-run trade on the street since 2020, so the 1.25 estimate is itself optimistic before slippage. Candidate 3 (vix_regime_dual_momo) is the worst of the three at PF 1.15 — well below floor — and the critic explicitly called it "not novel" (Faber/ReSolve well-trodden) with parameter sprawl. Promoting any of these would repeat the exact failure mode in memory `project-money-ready-2026-05-31.md` (money-ready bottleneck is plumbing/edge-quality, not adding more sub-T2 strategies) and `project-etf-pilot-day1-2026-06-02.md` (only one ETF strategy currently clears Tier-2 at PF 1.60; adding PF~1.2 noise dilutes the pilot). Per CLAUDE.md Goal #1, Tier-2 minimum is PF>1.5 — even the optimistic proposed PFs (1.55-1.70) are at-the-line, and the critic-adjusted reality is solidly sub-T2.
winners.risk_summary: Promoting a sub-PF-1.3 ETF strategy adds source-diversity theatre without real edge and will burn the n-budget on the live pilot. But 1.15 is still below the T2 floor (PF 1.5) and below the minimum bar (1.3). Given (a) FOREX is currently FAILing at PF 0.55 with n=53, (b) the Major Goal #1 banner requires hedge-fund-tier numbers, and (c) the policy_freeze exists precisely because we keep wiring sub-edge FX strategies, shipping any of these to live sizing would repeat the failure pattern. Recommendation: pilot #2 as a research candidate ONLY (paper, no size) with the FRED yield-lag fix baked into the data pipeline before any backtest is considered admissible.

Core failure modes are structural to retail FX: (a) execution costs (1-2 pip spreads + fix-window widening) eat small mean-reversion edges; (b) regime-router overfit risk is high when prior n=28; (c) carry-momentum has decayed since 2010 crowding and is exposed to carry-unwind tail events (Aug 2024 JPY unwind cost similar books ~12% in a week, the 4-week kill switch lags). winners.why_winner: All three candidates fail the hard gate of realistic PF >= 1.3. The critic's adjusted PF for all three is 1.15, which is below the required threshold and within noise of break-even after realistic commodity-specific frictions (borrow costs on short ETF legs, roll-yield decay, slippage on softs, deferred-contract data gaps via yfinance). Candidate 1 (cointegration reversion) has the most defensible mechanism but its realistic PF 1.15 already prices in borrow/slippage erosion of 25-35%, leaving no margin if ag-pair borrow proves prohibitive. Candidate 2 (term-structure carry) has a documented silent-degradation failure mode — yfinance deferred contracts unreliable, collapsing it to a TSMOM clone with n<100. Candidate 3 (HMM regime) is explicitly flagged high-overfit with 7-parameter stack on ~30-80 trades/yr — DoF/sample ratio is structurally bad and realistic WR 36% on a regime strategy is suspicious. Per CLAUDE.md M-107, we pre-register only strategies with realistic PF>=1.3; promoting any of these would repeat the SI=F / CT=F concentration-failure pattern that froze the class. Recommend running a smaller targeted experiment on Candidate 1 with hardened filters before re-proposing.

winners.why_winner: All three candidates fail the minimum bar of realistic PF >= 1.3 under critic adjustment — every one lands at PF ~1.15, which is below the required threshold and well inside the noise band for a class with n=0 history and known resolver contamination. Beyond the PF shortfall: (1) bond_duration_residual_mean_reversion has a structural flaw — applying DGS10 duration-residuals to credit-driven LQD/HYG systematically biases eR and reproduces the exact failure mode that killed prior BOND attempts; net margin per win (~20-40bps) is too thin for honest slippage. (2) bond_yield_curve_slope_momentum is flagged HIGH overfit with a heavy parameter stack (63d/20d ROC, ±5bp/±10bp slope thresholds, vol filter, VIX gates, 2/4 ATR, weekly rerank) on only ~4 distinct rate regimes since 2010 and a 9-ETF universe — the hand-tuned slope-bucket routing is unlikely to survive walk-forward, and realistic WR 42% on a momentum spec already sits at the low end of plausible. (3) bond_hmm_macro_regime_rotation is HIGH overfit with a 4-state HMM + 5 features + weekly refit producing only 8-15 trades/yr/sleeve, plus FRED vintage/revision leakage that will inflate backtest WR by 3-5pp vs live; n>=100 milestone takes ~7 years. Given BOND is already policy-frozen (n=0, no live pipeline) and the broader repo has an unresolved intrabar resolver contamination issue (per project memory), greenlighting any of these would generate yet another artifact-prone INSUFFICIENT_DATA sleeve rather than a real edge. Better to defer until the resolver is fixed and to seed BOND with a simpler, lower-parameter signal (e.g. plain 12-1 absolute momentum on TLT/IEF/HYG/TIP/BIL with a single VIX>35 cash gate) that has fewer DoF and can clear the PF 1.3 bar honestly.

winners.why_winner: All three candidates fail the realistic PF >= 1.3 bar after adversarial critique: gap_fade (PF 1.15), carry-momentum (PF 1.10), regime-switch (PF 1.05). The common root cause is data-feed fragility — yfinance continuous front-month (=F) tickers do not provide a clean F2 series, month-coded contracts (CLM26, ZCN26) are sparse/stale especially for ags and FX, and ETF proxies (USO/GLD/UNG) carry their own contango drag that biases the slope estimator. Since term-structure is the SOLE source of novelty distinguishing each candidate from the incumbent losing multi_asset_scanner, when the carry/slope leg silently degrades the strategy collapses back to a plain momentum or gap scanner — which is exactly the pattern already failing in production (9% WR, 100% src_conc on CL=F). Candidate #2 (carry+momentum) has the strongest academic backing (Moskowitz/Pedersen, Koijen) and lowest overfit, but at PF 1.10 net of slippage it does not justify lifting the freeze. Candidate #3 has 9 tunable knobs on n<100 — overfit too high. Candidate #1 is closest to viable (PF 1.15, hard intraday exits genuinely address the overnight-gap kill mode) but still under the bar. Recommendation: solve the data problem first (CME settlement-file ingest for true F1/F2 OHLC, or Norgate continuous adjusted series) before re-tournamenting FUTURES; without a reliable curve feed no term-structure strategy can be honestly backtested.
winners.recommended_first_step: Before re-running a FUTURES tournament: ship `tools/data/cme_settlement_ingest.py` to pull official CME daily settlement files (or wire Norgate/CSI continuous-adjusted series) into a new `futures_curve` table providing clean F1/F2/F3 OHLC + days-to-expiry per symbol per day. Then re-run candidate #1 (gap_fade_term_structure) as the lowest-overfit, most-implementable option via `verified_strategies/strategy_verification_engine.py` on the 10-symbol universe with a 90-day OOS walk-forward, and only consider lifting the FUTURES freeze if real-data PF >= 1.3 and src_conc <= 0.30.
winners.risk_summary: Primary risk is data-feed integrity: yfinance cannot deliver a clean futures curve, so any term-structure-conditioned strategy backtests will be optimistic on the symbols where F2 is missing/sparse (8/10 for #1, 3/4 sectors for #2, 4/4 complexes for #3 since ETF proxies bias the slope). Secondary risk is roll-day artifacts on the F1 continuous series itself, which manufactured the losses in the incumbent multi_asset_scanner and will recur unless explicitly detected. Tertiary risk is n-accumulation cadence: weekly rebalancing or STAND-DOWN regimes mean ~6 months of forward paper before n>=100 per M-107, so even a winning candidate cannot lift the FUTURES freeze quickly.
